advisory.finding: The SSRF guard in `_reject_private_resolution` resolves the target host via `getaddrinfo` and validates the resulting IPs are globally routable, but `opener.open()` subsequently performs its OWN independent DNS resolution and connection. The validated address set is not pinned to the address actually connected to, so a DNS-rebinding (or fast round-robin / short-TTL) response can pass the pre-check with a public IP and then serve a private/internal IP (e.g. 169.254.169.254 cloud metadata, 127.0.0.1) to the real connection — the exact SSRF the guard is meant to stop.
advisory.suggested_fix: Resolve the host once, validate every returned address, then connect using the validated IP (custom opener/HTTPSConnection bound to the checked address with SNI/Host preserved), or re-validate the peer address post-connect and abort on a non-global peer.
